topic: Animated title-screen Scourge, birds, and bees
currentUserGoal: Keep the beloved wholesome title artwork while making the scene more alive and showing ominous Scourge clouds slowly replace the blue sky, with birds and bees moving through the landscape.
workCompleted: Added a deterministic 42-second title atmosphere cycle that begins mostly clear, brews to full Scourge cover over about eighteen seconds, holds briefly, then releases the sky before repeating.
Added a multiply-blended sky veil and five layered, slowly drifting Scourge cloud banks with muted violet storm color and subtle pink fissures.
Added five distant birds with two generated wing poses, alternating travel direction, bobbing flight, and reduced visibility as the Scourge strengthens.
Added four animated bees using the existing pixel bee asset, with independent wandering flight paths, buzzing scale, direction changes, and gentle rotation.
Kept all title actors pooled and allocation-free during update; runtime textures are generated once and reused across title-scene visits.
Added responsive animation budgets: desktop uses at most 5 clouds, 5 birds, and 4 bees; phone uses 3 clouds, 3 birds, and 2 bees.
Preserved the existing background parallax, breathing, pollen motes, selectors, title layout, menus, credits, and audio behavior.
Added pure atmosphere timing and viewport-budget tests.
verificationRun: npm run check passed after the final motion tuning: ESLint, 200 Vitest tests across 24 files, strict TypeScript, and the Vite production build.
The local public title route returned HTTP 200.
Tests enforce the clear-to-full-to-clear Scourge cycle and bounded desktop, tablet, and phone actor counts.
Visual browser verification remains blocked by the in-app browser localhost URL policy, so the final layering and taste judgment require a user refresh.
git diff --check passed apart from normal Windows LF-to-CRLF notices.

gitStatus.expectedAfterCommit: Title-atmosphere checkpoint committed locally on top of the unpushed early-field pacing checkpoint; master should be two commits ahead of origin/master.

knownIssues: The generated clouds, birds, and bee paths compile and are bounded, but their final visual balance against the title artwork needs the user's hands-on judgment.
The Scourge is intentionally cyclical so the wholesome sky returns; this can be changed to a one-way takeover if the repeating story feels too gentle.
The title animation is local only until explicitly pushed and deployed.
nextRecommendedSteps: Refresh the local root title screen and remain on it for at least twenty-five seconds to watch the full Scourge build and hold.
Check that birds remain readable in the upper sky, bees are noticeable without crossing important menu copy, and storm cover feels ominous without obscuring the artwork.
Tune cloud darkness, cycle duration, or wildlife size from hands-on feedback, then push and deploy with the early-field pacing commit when approved.
doNotRevert: Do not replace the wholesome title background; the Scourge is a separate reversible overlay by design.
Do not turn the atmospheric actors into per-frame allocations, particles, or unbounded tweens.
Do not increase phone actor counts without measuring the public title route.
Do not include docs/CODEX_GITHUB_SETUP_GUIDE.md in this checkpoint without explicit user direction.
